# Methods Overview

Last updated: 2026-10-08 (stale-fact pass: host references, catalog counts, payloads, publish gates)
Scope: the Method layer as it exists today — what each method does, how a method run is wired
end to end, and where the layer is still unfinished, functionally and aesthetically.

This is an orientation document, not a spec. It records the current state so the revision work
that follows has a shared starting point. Related documents: `docs/final-steps/product/METHODS_ARETE_INSTRUCTION_BLUEPRINT.md`
(older inventory, now partly stale), `docs/final-steps/quality/METHOD_RUNTIME_QA_CHECKLIST.md`, `docs/final-steps/product/POINTS_SYSTEM.md`,
`docs/final-steps/product/Paths_Design_Guide.md`.

## 1. What a method is

A pattern answers *what* the user committed to. A method answers *how the app watches it happen*.
Every template and user pattern carries exactly one method, and that method decides which screen
opens when the user performs the pattern, what the user does on that screen, and what artifact —
if any — the run leaves behind.

The method is therefore the only place in the app where a commitment turns into evidence. Everything
downstream (points, streaks, badges, the social feed, Arete's view of the user) inherits whatever
the method chose to record.

## 3. Catalog

Nine live methods, one retired (`learnWithAreteMethod`, kept only for decoding old submissions),
plus an `undefined` fallback. `Methods.undefined` decodes from any unknown raw value and renders
`TakeNotesMethod`, so a bad payload degrades to a working screen rather than a placeholder.

| Method | Screen | Lines | Proof payload | Template patterns using it |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `takePictureMethod` | `Media/TakePictureMethod.swift` | 1792 | `image` (uploaded URLs) | 26 |
| `registerAudioMethod` | `Media/RegisterAudioMethod.swift` | 1018 | `audio` (uploaded URLs) | 2 |
| `takeNotesMethod` | `Media/TakeNotesMethod.swift` | 420 | `text` (the note itself, stored inline) | 4 |
| `drawPaintingMethod` | `Media/DrawPaintingMethod.swift` | 1925 | `image` (composed export) | 1 |
| `wakeUpMethod` | `Physical/WakeUpMethod.swift` | 501 | check-in record typed `text` (window, check-in time, observed alarm alert and dismissal) + `alarmSound` | 1 |
| `trackMotionMethod` | `Physical/TrackMotionMethod.swift` | 869 | `map` (route, distance, speed, steps, estimated calories) | 7 |
| `countPushupsMethod` | `Physical/CountPushupsMethod.swift` | 1473 | `float` (valid reps, or held seconds for a plank) + per-rep or per-hold evidence | 4 |
| `readBooksMethod` | `Learning/ReadBooksMethod.swift` | 2746 | structured session record typed `text` (book, start and end progress, active reader seconds; no written summary) | 1 |
| `learnWithAreteMethod` **(retired)** | `Learning/LearnWithAreteMethod.swift` | 1084 | `text` (conversation transcript) | 0 |
| `playGamesMethod` | `Games/PlayGamesMethod.swift` | 730 | `text` (game, outcome and score) | 1 |
| `undefined` | falls back to Take Notes | — | — | 0 |

`learnWithAreteMethod` is retired (`Paths/Models/Patterns/PatternRetirement.swift`): filtered out
of new-pattern selection, kept only so existing users' past submissions still decode. Treat it as
nine live methods, not ten, for any forward-looking work.

Two numbers are worth holding onto. The layer is roughly 19,000 lines across 39 Swift files, and
more than half the bundled catalog (26 of 47 patterns) routes into a single method, Take Picture.
Any change to Take Picture is a change to the majority of the product's surface area; the long tail
of methods carries one or two patterns each and is comparatively under-exercised.

## 4. Anatomy of a run

1. **Selection.** The user opens a scheduled pattern in the calendar. `PerformPattern` resolves the
   `UserPattern` and its `PatternInstance` and pushes `PerformPatternRoute.method`.
2. **Instantiation.** `MethodViewFactory.createMethodView(for:userPattern:patternInstance:)` switches
   on the enum and returns the screen with six environment objects attached — `UserPattern`,
   `PatternInstance`, `TimeManager`, `AudioManager`, `ControlState`, `CalendarManager`. The
   `withMethodEnvironment` modifier exists so a method can never crash on a missing environment object.
3. **Session start (Methods Lab only).** The debug Methods Lab host in `CoreFlow` (`MethodsLabRootView`)
   opens a proof session on appear and closes it on disappear, and puts the proof lab behind a single
   toolbar badge so the method's own layout is never displaced by instrumentation. The production host
   in `PerformPattern` opens no proof session.
4. **Performance.** The method screen runs its own capture, timing, permission and session-restore
   logic. Almost all of that logic lives inside the method file itself.
5. **Publish.** The method's `prepareSubmission` writes `content` and `dataType` into
   `patternInstance.dates[ddMMyyyy]` and uploads any binary to Supabase storage, refusing (mostly with
   `MethodSubmissionError.missingEvidence`) when there is nothing to submit. The shared
   `PublishMethodContentButton` then stamps `timePublished`, sets `didIt = true` and syncs the instance
   with `updatePatternInstanceInSupabase`.
6. **Reward.** Points arithmetic happens server-side in the `award_progress_points_secure` RPC;
   there is deliberately no client-side `addPoints` (see the comment at `Paths/Models/Progress/Levels.swift:429`).

`PerformPattern` also owns a lifecycle-automation completion path that publishes an instance without
opening a method at all (`PerformPattern.swift:347`). That path writes the same shape of payload with
`content = "Lifecycle automation completion"`.

## 5. Proof: what is instrumented and what is not

The Method Proof Lab is the half-built machinery for making completion mean something. Its own header
comments state the problem plainly: a completion today is a button tap — `didIt = true`, points, no evidence.

- `Proof/MethodProofSignals.swift` is the recorder. Methods call
  `MethodProofRecorder.shared.record(...)` unconditionally; outside the Lab there is no open session,
  so the call is a no-op. Signals are graded on a four-tier scale — **A attested**, **B artifact**,
  **C attention**, **D declared** — with the stated design rule that every method must reach artifact
  or attested, that attention can support a contract but never carry it, and that a bare tap earns nothing.
- `Proof/MethodProofRules.swift` is the judge. A rule is a set of clauses so a failing run can say
  *which* clause failed. **Only `takePictureMethod` has a rule.** Every other method reports as
  uninstrumented, which the file notes is deliberate — the Lab should not imply a contract exists
  where it does not.
- `Proof/MethodProofLabPanel.swift` is the operator surface, presented as a sheet from the toolbar badge.
- `Proof/PhotoEvidenceAnalyzer.swift` backs the picture clauses.

**Current instrumentation coverage: one method of ten.** `TakePictureMethod` records photos required,
photos captured, picture mode, expected subject, and pre-existing photos (`TakePictureMethod.swift:527-614`).
No other method calls the recorder at all, so their Lab sessions are empty by construction.

Nothing in the Lab gates real completion yet. Thresholds are meant to be set from observed runs before
they gate anything, and that evidence has not been gathered.

## 6. What each method can do today

**Take Picture.** Detects a picture mode from pattern context — food, living space, single, or general
*N*-photo — and resolves a capture template. Only three guide shapes exist; per-pattern silhouettes were
tried and dropped because the guide, the preview, the crop and the artwork all had to agree and any
drift misled the user about what was being kept. Custom artwork fills the empty state only, resolved by
slug through `CustomCutoutAssetResolver` (`capture_guide_<slug>`); 20 such imagesets ship in
`Assets.xcassets`, with sources in `Methods_Images/`. Its Complete button is template-driven: it stays
disabled until the capture template's required photo count (1, 2 or 4 by pattern) is met for today.
Every method gates Complete on evidence presence; none of them on evidence quality: a note needs text,
a drawing a stroke or shape, audio a recording, a motion session recorded movement (distance, steps or
floors), a pose session a valid rep or hold, reading open text and active reading time, a game a
finished game, and Wake Up a check-in inside the 30 minutes after the rest interval.

**Register Audio.** AAC/M4A recording with a live waveform, timer, a multi-recording queue, playback with
seek and skip. `AudioManager` (the shared environment object) lives inside this file.

**Take Notes.** Freeform text with an undo/redo manager, keyboard-aware layout, and a poem-type picker.
Also the fallback screen for `undefined`.

**Draw & Paint.** PencilKit canvas with layers, brush and eraser tools, text tools, zoom, backgrounds,
reference images, export and share. Prompts can be generated through `AnthropicChatService`
(`DrawingPromptGenerator.swift:66`). Split across ten files, the widest decomposition in the layer.

**Wake Up.** Alarm readiness: sound picker, permission/battery/volume checklist, looping preview alarm.
At check-in, inside the 30 minutes after the rest interval, it publishes a check-in record typed `text`
(window, check-in time, observed alarm alert and dismissal) plus the chosen sound.

**Track Motion.** GPS route, HealthKit, pedometer; distance, speed, steps, calories, and a polyline
persisted as a `map` payload. Owns `HealthKitManager` and `LocationManager`.

**Count Pushups.** Vision-based pose tracking with phase detection, calibration flow, per-rep quality
badges, and a session comparison panel. `poseLockHealthy` gates calibration and the start of the
counted set, not Complete; Complete needs at least one valid rep (or held seconds for a plank).

**Read Books.** Gutenberg search and library, chapter model, reading themes and fonts, bookmarks,
session persistence. The largest single method file. It publishes a structured session record (book,
start and end progress, active reader seconds), not a written summary.

**Learn with Arete (retired).** Chat against `AreteService` with a conversation context, attachments, a
learning profile form, and a setup guide. Published the transcript; kept only so past submissions decode.

**Play Games.** Chess, Go and Sudoku, each backed by an engine in `Paths/Models/Games/`, reporting
outcome and move count through an `onComplete` callback into a day summary.

## 7. Aesthetic state

Most method screens have been converted to the design system — `PathsColor`, `PathsFont`, `PathsSpacing`,
`PathsRadius` — and the conversion is uneven rather than absent. Counting design-token references against
raw `.font(.system(...)` / literal-color usage per file:

- **Clean:** Read Books, Learn with Arete, Learning Profile, Take Picture, Play Games, Count Pushups,
  Wake Up, Take Notes, Register Audio, the game boards.
- **Mixed:** Draw & Paint, Setup Guide, Enhanced Pose Overlay, Drawing Backgrounds, Drawing Models,
  Media Capture Styles, Embedded Camera Preview.
- **Unconverted:** `MethodProofLabPanel.swift` — 40 raw font/color usages, zero tokens. It is an
  instrument rather than a product surface, so this is defensible for now, but it is the one screen
  that looks like a different app.

Extracted style files exist for three areas only — `PushupMethodStyles`, `MethodMotionStyles`,
`MethodMediaCaptureStyles`, `DrawingStyles` — so most method styling still sits inline in the method
file, against the repo's own modularization pattern.

## 8. Open revision agenda

### Functional

1. **Proof coverage.** Nine of ten methods record nothing. Until they do, the tier scale is aspiration
   rather than measurement, and no threshold can be set from evidence.
2. **Rules coverage.** One rule exists. Each remaining method needs a completion contract that has been
   watched to succeed on an honest run and fail on a faked one.
3. **Gating.** No rule gates real completion. The decision of when the Lab stops being an observer is
   still open, and it interacts directly with the skip / add-time allowance work — forgiveness and proof
   are the two dials on the same mechanism.
4. **Coverage imbalance.** 26 of 47 template patterns use Take Picture. Either more methods earn
   patterns, or Take Picture's modes need to carry more distinct experiences than four.
5. **File size.** Five live method files exceed 1,000 lines (six with the retired Learn with Arete) and
   one, Read Books, exceeds 2,000. Read Books, Take Picture and Count Pushups each mix capture, session,
   persistence and presentation in one file.
6. **Shared publish path.** The `didIt` flip, publish stamp and sync now live once in
   `PublishMethodContentButton.publishContent()`; each method still writes its own `dates[dateKey]`
   content and upload in `prepareSubmission`. That seam is the natural place for a proof gate.
7. **Session restore.** Restore behavior differs per method and is not specified anywhere; the runtime
   QA checklist covers only drawing, picture and audio.
8. **The `undefined` fallback.** Rendering Take Notes for an unknown method is safe, but it silently
   changes what the user is asked to do. Worth deciding whether that should be visible.

### Aesthetic

1. **Finish the token conversion** in Draw & Paint, Setup Guide, and the pose overlay.
2. **Extract inline styles** into per-method `*Styles.swift` files, matching the pattern already used
   in Physical and Media.
3. **Unify the method chrome.** Title treatment, time-remaining presentation and the Complete affordance
   differ per method; they should read as one family before the individual screens are polished.
4. **Decide the Proof Lab's visual status** — permanently an instrument, or a surface that eventually
   ships to users.
5. **Capture guide artwork** covers 20 of the 26 picture patterns, with no orphaned assets. Missing:
   Eat a healthy dinner, Clean your living space, Take photos, Visit a new place, Try new cuisine,
   Visit a museum. Complete the set, or make the empty state work without artwork.
6. **Game boards** (Chess, Go, Sudoku) use tokens but were built independently and do not yet read as
   one visual system.
